articles.title: Mumbai Indians appoint Kieron Pollard as head coach ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard will take charge of Mumbai Indians as head coach ahead of IPL 2027.
articles.body: Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard will take charge of Mumbai Indians as head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The five-time IPL champions announced the appointment on Saturday, with Pollard replacing Mahela Jayawardene.Pollard has been working as Mumbai Indians' batting coach for the past few seasons. The franchise has now promoted him to the top coaching role, continuing its long association with the former West Indies T20 captain."Mumbai Indians are pleased to announce the elevation of Kieron Pollard to Head Coach, extending one of the most enduring player-to-coach associations in cricket," MI said in a statement.MI look to build on their legacyMumbai Indians said Pollard's appointment was part of their plan to build on the team's success, develop young players and maintain their winning culture."Pollard's appointment reflects Mumbai Indians' commitment to building on the team's legacy while continuing to develop talent, strengthen its culture and pursue excellence on and off the field.""His leadership will be rooted in the experience of having been part of MI's most successful years, alongside the ambition to shape the team's next chapter," the franchise said.MI are among the most successful teams in IPL history, having won the title five times. However, their last championship came in 2020. One of Pollard's biggest challenges will be to help the team end its title drought.Pollard speaks about his bond with MIPollard said Mumbai Indians had played a major role in his career and that he understood the responsibility of leading the team."MI has been a huge part of my life and career, and the bond I share with this team, the players and the Paltan means a great deal to me," Pollard said in a statement shared by the franchise."Having experienced this journey as a player and then as a coach, I understand what Mumbai Indians stands for and the responsibility that comes with representing the Blue and Gold," he added.Pollard's record with Mumbai IndiansThe 39-year-old has played in franchise T20 leagues around the world. In the IPL, however, he represented only Mumbai Indians, from 2009-10 until his final appearance in the 2022 edition.Pollard also represented MI New York in Major League Cricket this year.In 189 IPL matches for Mumbai Indians, Pollard scored 3,412 runs at an average of 28.67 and a strike rate of 147.32. His record includes 16 half-centuries. He also took 69 wickets, with his best figures being 4/44.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ, 2nd T20I: Tilak, Nitish star as India pull off stunning chase to beat New Zealand by 4 wickets
articles.body: India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd T20I: Squads India: Shreyas Iyer (c), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma (vc), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav, Kumar Kushagra (wk). New Zealand: Mitchell Santner (c), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Zak Foulkes, Matt Henry, Bevon Jacobs, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith.India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd T20I: New Zealand spinners could hold the key While the Indian batters dominated the powerplay, New Zealand spinners Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell made life difficult for them in the middle overs. India's left-handed batters have shown vulnerability against off-spin, a weakness Bracewell was able to exploit in the first match. New Zealand will look to build on that success and put pressure on India's middle order. However, with India's batting depth, the hosts will need a much stronger bowling effort to level the series..India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd T20I: New Zealand also need to tighten their bowling India are not the only team looking for improvements. New Zealand's bowlers also struggled to contain the visitors in the opening match. Pacers Matt Henry and Adam Milne found swing early in their spells but could not consistently trouble Samson and Abhishek Sharma with their lengths. The Indian openers took full advantage, scoring 94 runs in the powerplay and putting New Zealand on the back foot. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said his team would need to find a way to slow down India's in-form top order. "So I think both teams could probably look at a few things here and there, which I think could have gone either way. The extras at the start maybe and obviously I think in the field we were pretty good," said Santner. "It's not an easy ground to catch here. A couple of more chances, closing overs at times, but, I think the powerplay is always going to be a challenge. I guess we have to find a way to slow them down (Samson and Abhishek)," he added..India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd T20I: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi likely to open The second T20I could offer fans a chance to watch 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi bat in the middle. Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the match due to injury, with Kumar Kushagra joining the squad as his replacement. Sooryavanshi is expected to open alongside Abhishek Sharma, while Sanju Samson could bat at number three. Tilak Varma is likely to return to his usual number five position after moving up the order in the first match because of Kishan's injury..India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd T20I: Shreyas Iyer wants bowlers to get their lengths right India captain Shreyas Iyer admitted that his bowlers failed to hit the right lengths in the first match. "...we bowled a little ahead compared to the hard lengths we should have been hitting," acknowledged India skipper Shreyas Iyer after the four-wicket win in which his 28-ball 42 proved vital. Axar Patel will also be keen to improve after conceding the most runs among India's bowlers in the series opener. The conditions in Christchurch are expected to favour batters again, leaving little room for mistakes..India vs New Zealand Live Score: India need better performance from bowling attack India’s fifth and sixth bowling options remain a concern, especially with all-rounders yet to make a strong impact in the absence of Hardik Pandya. In the series opener, Nitish Kumar Reddy conceded 40 runs in four overs without taking a wicket. Naman Dhir did not get an opportunity to bowl before making a match-winning contribution with the bat. India’s regular bowlers also struggled. Bhuvneshwar Kumar, playing his first match for India in nearly four years, conceded 49 runs in his four overs. He also bowled two no-balls and two wides. New Zealand openers Finn Allen and Tim Seifert attacked Bhuvneshwar and Arshdeep Singh during the powerplay, putting both bowlers under pressure..India vs New Zealand Live Score: Hello and welcome! Hello and welcome to the LIVE coverage of the second T20I between India and New Zealand at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch. India’s batters came to the rescue in the first T20I, helping the team chase down 226 runs and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. However, the bowlers have plenty to work on ahead of the second match in Christchurch on Saturday. New Zealand’s aggressive batting exposed India’s weaknesses with the ball. With another batting-friendly pitch expected, the visitors will need to improve their performance to stop the hosts from scoring freely.

articles.title: 'Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar credits IPL for India comeback
articles.summary: India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work without expecting too much from himself helped him deal with a four-year absence from
articles.body: India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work without expecting too much from himself helped him deal with a four-year absence from international cricket. The experienced bowler returned to the national setup earlier this month as a replacement for injured Arshdeep Singh in the fifth T20I against the West Indies, but rain washed out the match. He eventually returned to action in the first T20I against New Zealand.Speaking in a video shared by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), Bhuvneshwar explained that focusing on the present instead of worrying about a comeback helped him grow as a player and person.“The headspace I am in is very simple. I have no expectations of myself. I think that’s how things worked out for me in the last 3-4 years. No expectations; just keep doing your work. Generally, we talk about being present; we don’t think about the future. I think that’s the headspace I am in right now. And that has happened in the last 3-4 years,” he said.Bhuvneshwar said the years away from international cricket taught him patience and maturity. Rather than constantly chasing a place in the Indian team, he concentrated on improving his game through the IPL and domestic cricket.“Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey. So honestly, I didn’t even know when those four years would come. I think it evolved big time, and I think IPL has a big role in that.”Despite having no clear expectations about his future, the 36-year-old continued working on his fitness, skills and mental preparation. He also expressed surprise at winning two IPL titles in two years.Adapting to modern T20 cricketBhuvneshwar acknowledged that T20 cricket has changed considerably, with batters attacking from the first ball and scores of 200 becoming increasingly common. However, he believes bowlers can still control the game by using smart strategies and making batters hit where they want.He also pointed out that overseas tours, particularly to SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), present challenges because conditions often offer limited help to bowlers. According to him, success in these conditions requires maturity, careful planning and teamwork.Reflecting on India's opening win against New Zealand, Bhuvneshwar said a strong start could boost confidence across the squad and help the team perform better throughout the tour and in other formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second T20 International on Saturday.
articles.body: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second T20 International on Saturday.India made two changes to their playing XI. Injured Ishan Kishan was replaced by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, while Prince Yadav came in for Mayank Yadav.Iyer confirmed that Sooryavanshi would bat at No. 3 and not open the innings. India will continue with Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson as their opening pair.Iyer explains India's decision to bowlIyer said the possibility of dew was one of the reasons behind India's decision to bowl first. He also stressed the need to maintain the aggressive approach that helped the team in the first T20I."We're going to bowl first. Yes, absolutely. That's one of the reasons (On dew being a factor). We have had a little bit of time to recover and catch up on some sleep. Everyone is in decent shape, I would say. Some of the players, including myself, do their training on match day. So, we are in a good place. It is important to maintain the aggression and repeat the things we did well in the first game," Shreyas Iyer said during the toss.The Indian captain also pointed out the need to improve the team's fielding and avoid mistakes in the final overs."In addition, we need to be proactive in the field and ensure we don't have an extra fielder inside the circle, especially in the last over. Ishan is injured, so Vaibhav comes in for him. Prince comes in for Mayank, which is just a tactical change. He is going to bat at number three (on Vaibhav's batting position)," the Indian skipper said.New Zealand make one changeNew Zealand also made a change to their playing XI, with Jacob Duffy replacing Adam Milne.Captain Mitchell Santner said his team had taken positives from the first T20I despite losing the match in the final over. He added that the team needed to improve its execution in key moments."(On the 1st T20I) They are a very good team, and I think we missed the mark slightly. That comes from the way they approach their game. It was a great game of cricket in the end. Losing in the last over is disappointing, but there were obviously many positives. We need to execute the small details better and see what happens," Mitchell Santner said.Santner said the players had been given time to rest after returning to their hotel late at night. With matches coming thick and fast, the team wanted to make sure everyone was ready for the second T20I."(On the preparation for this match) Training was optional. We had a morning session, and we only got back here around 2 a.m. Therefore, it was a day to refresh, especially with the games coming thick and fast. I think the guys rested well and should be ready to go today," he said.The New Zealand captain also explained that Duffy's inclusion was part of the team's rotation policy and was not linked to Milne's performance."(On the changes) Duffy comes in for Milne. With the number of games we have coming up, not just T20s but one-day internationals as well, there will be some rotation among the senior players, especially with a lot of Test cricket coming up. It is nothing to do with performance; it is just a bit of rotation, and we will see what Duffy can do tonight," Santner added.India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I: Playing XIsIndia: Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav.New Zealand: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their development program, TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The 52-year-old will work with MI's development squad alongside Zubin Bharucha, who has joined the five-time champions as director of performance, earlier this year.Jones, who also served as Rajasthan Royals' fast-bowling coach during the 2019 edition of the IPL, was later brought back by the franchise as its high-performance fast-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2022.It is also learnt that Bharucha and Jones have a specific role: to work with Indian players during the ongoing domestic season.Jones, who played first-class cricket in the English county circuit between 1997 and 2011, recently worked with India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy. The Welshman helped the youngster improve his bowling speed. Reddy, who used to bowl in the mid-120s, is now consistently clocking the mid-130s.Earlier on Saturday, MI roped in Kieron Pollard as their head coach, replacing Mahela Jayawardene. The franchise is likely to take the big call on captaincy and movement is expected on Hardik Pandya trade in the coming weeks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘You did nothing wrong’: Faf du Plessis reveals message to Steve Smith during Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy, questioning why
articles.body: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy, questioning why the Australian had taken responsibility for the incident while expressing solidarity with a rival who had previously stood by him during his own ball-tampering scandal.Speaking on Cricinfo’s Cricketers on Cricketers, du Plessis said Smith’s response to the controversy had reminded him of the media storm he faced in 2016, when he was accused of using residue from a sweet to alter the condition of the ball during a Test against Australia in Hobart.Smith, Australia's captain at the time, was at the centre of a major controversy during the 2018 tour of South Africa after Cameron Bancroft was caught attempting to alter the ball's condition with sandpaper in the Cape Town Test. Smith and vice-captain David Warner were also found guilty of their roles in the incident."Steve came out at the end of the day [in Cape Town in 2018] saying: 'I take responsibility.' And we were like: 'Why are you taking responsibility? You did nothing wrong,'" du Plessis said.‘We're behind you’: Faf's message to SmithDu Plessis said he immediately empathised with Smith as the controversy escalated and the Australian faced intense media scrutiny. Drawing parallels with his own experience, the former South African skipper sent Smith a message of support, assuring him that he understood the pressure he was going through."And then everything just exploded in terms of the media and how he was being put under pressure. Straight away, I was like: this is not his doing. This is the same thing [as my ball-tampering charge]. I remember sending a message and saying: 'Listen, I'm so sorry you are going through this. Just be strong. It's going to be a hell for a week or so and then it will probably blow over.' Never knowing that it was going to be a year for him to go through. But just saying… we're behind you. We understand you did nothing wrong. So if you need anything from us, we're here," he told Cricinfo.The former South Africa captain admitted he had not anticipated the severity of the punishment that would follow, with Cricket Australia eventually imposing one-year suspensions on Smith and Warner and removing Smith from the captaincy. Bancroft received a nine-month ban, while the International Cricket Council handed Smith a one-Test suspension.Smith had stood by Faf during ‘Mintgate’Du Plessis also recalled how Smith had defended him during the 2016 Hobart controversy, when accusations of cheating began to spread internationally. The South African said the situation had initially appeared relatively minor to his dressing room, before the growing media attention turned it into a major issue."At the time, in our dressing room, honestly, we thought nothing had happened badly. But cameras [were] everywhere. And it just got built up into this thing now. All of a sudden, I was in real trouble. It was going around the world, people saying, 'Cheating.' That weighs heavy on you,” he said.According to du Plessis, Smith was asked about the allegations against the South African and chose to defend him, despite the pressure surrounding the issue.“He was asked: What are your thoughts on Faf du Plessis and Mintgate, and it's terrible, he's cheating. And he's like, no, he's not. He's just shining the ball. I've been on many teams where we shine the ball, we use different sweets. We were listening to it on the TV and literally everyone in our group was like, 'Wow, he doesn't have to do that.' That was a choice where he went: I'm going to choose probably the human, the right thing, versus the pressure thing. That was amazing for me to see. I remember just saying that that meant a lot to the South African team and the respect that we got for Steve Smith that day," he added.Du Plessis said Smith's willingness to speak up when he could have simply criticised his rival left a lasting impression on the South African camp.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
